evidence: Cic. Off. 3.1: nec minus sōlum quam cum sōlus esset
terms.comment: It agrees with the person: sōlus cēnō, I dine alone. Two together with no one else are sōlī (Aug. Conf. 9.10.23). For “the only one”, see only (the only one).

terms.gloss: solitary, alone by nature or habit
evidence: Cic. Amic. 88: sīc nātūra sōlitārium nihil amat
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: alone, by itself, lonely.

phrases.english: I don’t like dining alone, Fabullus

phrases.latin: dīc mihi, quis furor est? … sōlus bōlētōs, Caeciliāne, vorās
phrases.english: tell me, what madness is this? … you gobble the mushrooms all by yourself, Caecilianus
on my own I would never have done it

phrases.latin: numquam sē minus ōtiōsum esse quam cum ōtiōsus, nec minus sōlum quam cum sōlus esset
phrases.english: (he used to say) that he was never less idle than when at leisure, nor less alone than when he was alone

phrases.latin: dōnec eris sōspes, multōs numerābis amīcōs: tempora sī fuerint nūbila, sōlus eris
phrases.english: as long as you prosper you will count many friends; if the skies cloud over, you will be alone
so we talked together, alone, very sweetly

sources: Lewis & Short: solus · Lewis & Short: solitarius
